A 1992 constitutional amendment limited the governor to two terms, even if they are nonconsecutive, effective with the [[1994 Michigan gubernatorial election|1994 election]]. Engler's [[Lieutenant Governor of Michigan|lieutenant governor]] [[Dick Posthumus]], also a Republican, ran in his place. [[Jennifer Granholm]], then [[attorney general of Michigan]], ran on the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] ticket. [[James Blanchard]] (who was upset by Engler in [[1990 Michigan gubernatorial election|1990]]) and former [[Party whips of the United States House of Representatives|House Minority Whip]] [[David Bonior]]. Granholm was accused in the 2002 Democratic primary of several allegations of [[cronyism]]. Her husband, Daniel Mulhern, had received several contracts for his leadership training company shortly after Granholm left her position as Wayne County corporation counsel in 1998. He received nearly $300,000 worth of contracts, despite being the highest bidder for one of those contracts. Opponents criticized Granholm's supporters for engaging in cronyism and giving contracts to her husband immediately after leaving county employment.
